terminal.description: A terminal in your workspace. `node free-plots.js` lists the free plots once `plots.js` does the reading, and `node free-plots.js --row B` lists the free plots of row B.

tasks.title: Read the plot list in one module
tasks.description:
Write `plots.js` as a module that exports one async function, `readPlots(file)`. It reads the plot list at the path `file` and gives back an array with one object per plot, in the order of the file:

```js
[
  { plot: 'A1', holder: 'Maud Pask' },
  { plot: 'A3', holder: null }
]
```

A free plot has `holder: null`. Blank lines are not plots, and a list saved on Windows reads the same. Leave the printing to the scripts that import `plots.js`: they decide what to say.

Check imports `readPlots` from your `plots.js` in a script of its own, calls it on two lists of its own, and compares what it gives back.
nextSteps: Write `readPlots(file)` and put `export` in front of it.
Split the text into lines as before, and turn each into an object.
Give back the array, with `null` for a plot that has no holder.
hints: A module shares a function by exporting it. A function that uses `await` has `async` in front of it.
`export async function readPlots(file) { ... }`. Inside, read the file, split it with `/\r?\n/`, leave out blank lines and `map` each line to an object.
`.map((line) => { const [plot, holder] = line.split(','); return { plot, holder: holder === '' ? null : holder } })`.

tasks.title: List the free plots with readPlots
tasks.description:
Write `free-plots.js` so that `node free-plots.js` prints the name of every free plot in `plots.txt` beside the script, one per line, in the order of the list:

```
A3
B2
C3
```

It reads the list by importing `readPlots` from `plots.js`, not by reading the file itself. When no plot is free, it prints `No free plots.`

Check puts a stand-in `plots.js` of its own beside your script, so this task is judged on its own, and runs `free-plots.js` from two folders and with no free plot. The stand-in answers only for the `plots.txt` beside the scripts.
nextSteps: Import `readPlots` from your own module, by its path.
Call it with the path to `plots.txt` beside the script, and wait for it.
Keep the plots whose holder is `null`.
Print their names, or the line for when none are free.
hints: A file of your own is imported by a path that starts with `./` and ends with its `.js`.
`const free = plots.filter((p) => p.holder === null)`, then print `free.map((p) => p.plot).join('\n')`.

tasks.title: Print the version of the tools
tasks.description:
`package.json` describes the society's tools: their name, their version, and how Node should read their files. Write `version.js` so that `node version.js` prints the name and the version from `package.json` beside the script, with one space between:

```
marrowfield-tools 0.1.0
```

It works from any folder, and it reads the file as it is when the script runs.

Check puts a `package.json` of its own beside the script, with another name and version, and runs `version.js` from two folders.
nextSteps: Open `package.json` and find the two values you need.
Read it from the script's own folder.
Turn its text into an object.
Print the name, a space and the version.
hints: `package.json` is a JSON text file. The lesson shows two ways to get its contents as an object.
`JSON.parse(text)` turns the file's text into an object with `name` and `version` properties.

tasks.title: Show the free plots of one row
tasks.description:
Plots are named by row and number, so B2 is in row B. Add an option to `free-plots.js`: `node free-plots.js --row B` prints only the free plots whose name starts with `B`, one per line, or `No free plots.` when that row has none. With no option it lists every free plot, as in Task 2.

An option the script does not know, like `--colour red`, or `--row` with nothing after it, gets one plain line on standard error and exit code 1, and no plots. Read the options with `parseArgs` from `node:util`.

Check runs `free-plots.js` with the stand-in `plots.js` from Task 2 and options of its own, good and bad.
nextSteps: Describe the one option the script takes, `row`, which takes a value.
Catch the error `parseArgs` throws for an option it does not know.
Keep only the free plots whose name starts with the row, when one was given.
hints: `parseArgs` reads `process.argv` for you. It throws for an option you did not describe, and for an option that is missing its value.
`parseArgs({ options: { row: { type: 'string' } } }).values.row` is the letter, or `undefined` with no `--row`.
Wrap the `parseArgs` call in `try`; in the `catch`, `console.error(error.message)` and `process.exitCode = 1`. Then filter with `p.plot.startsWith(row)`.
